title: ai-playbook bundle config (v1)
description: Declarative bundle produced by tools/config-ui (HTML) and consumed by scripts/apply_config.py + scripts/bootstrap.py --from-config. Tri-category surface: rules{} (per-rule toggles + layers + advanced), features{} (installed components with state files + side effects — today only caveman), global_flags{} (binary env-driven toggles, no state file). Sparse: only modified-from-default entries appear. Sub-shapes are declarative intent only — the canonical state lives in per-feature files (.ai-playbook/rules-toggle.json, .ai-playbook/caveman.json, .ai-playbook/feature-flags.env), each gitignored.

generated_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp when the UI exported this bundle. Optional.

generated_by.description: Identifier of the agent/user that exported the bundle. Optional; UI defaults to 'anonymous' when no git user is detectable in-browser.

rules.description: Sparse map of rule-slug -> override. Same shape as schema-rules-toggle-v1.json's `rules` field; apply_config projects these into <consumer>/.ai-playbook/rules-toggle.json verbatim. Rules absent are inherited as fully-ON.

features.description: Installed features with their own state file + side effects. Only features explicitly modified appear here. apply_config delegates to each feature's CLI (e.g. `python -m scripts.caveman on/off`) to preserve materialisation + backups.

caveman.description: Caveman declarative intent. apply_config translates this to `python -m scripts.caveman on --mode X --components csv` or `off`. The canonical state lives at .ai-playbook/caveman.json (managed by the caveman CLI only; see schema-caveman-toggle-v1.json).

enabled.description: Master switch. When false, apply_config calls `caveman off` (strips AGENTS.md block + restores MCP wrappers).

mode.description: Intensity level for response_style. Consulted only when enabled=true.

global_flags.description: Binary env-driven toggles without their own state file. Keys come from tools/config-ui/global-flags-inventory.json. apply_config projects these into <consumer>/.ai-playbook/feature-flags.env via the inventory's env_var/value_on/value_off mapping. Consumer must source the file in their shell init (direnv .envrc, bashrc, etc.) for the flags to take effect.

skills_enforce.description: Per-skill enforcement choices. Negative-list (opt-out) shape: only `disabled` is persisted in the bundle. apply_config projects this section into <consumer>/.ai-playbook-state/skills-enforce.json (schema: skills-enforce/v1), and scripts/materialise_skills.py honours it on next materialise pass. Omitted ⇒ all skills enforced (default).

disabled.description: Skill slugs (directory names under skills/) that MUST NOT be materialised on this consumer.

mcps_enforce.description: Per-MCP-server enforcement choices. Negative-list (opt-out): only `disabled` is persisted. apply_config projects this section into <consumer>/.ai-playbook-state/mcps-enforce.json (schema: mcps-enforce/v1), and scripts/mcp/render.py + scripts/mcp/validate.py honour it on the next render/validate pass. Omitted ⇒ all servers enforced (default).

disabled.description: MCP server canonical IDs (the `id:` field in mcp-servers*.yaml) that MUST NOT be rendered into `.mcp.json` or `.gemini/settings.json` for this consumer.
